findings.text: the recorded base-arm command names tests/discovery/test_evaluation.py, which does not exist at the base revision caf9ab6d6, yet the log records '61 passed ... EXIT=0'; pytest exits 4 on an absent path argument, so the header cannot be the literal command that produced that output. The 61->74 delta is still sound (13 = the new file's tests), but the manifest's baseline_suite.command over-states the base arm's file set and is not reproducible as written.

test_interval_contains_its_point_estimate asserts out['point'] == ev.roc_auc(labels, scores), the bootstrap's internal point estimate against a direct call of the same function on the same inputs the test passed in; both sides are the code under test, so a roc_auc regression moves them together and the assertion stays green. It is a wiring check for bootstrap_interval only; the independent known answers live in TestRocAuc.

assert out['difference'] == out['auc_a'] - out['auc_b'] reads paired_auc's own returned dict on both sides, so it holds for any implementation that computes the difference from its own two calls; it guards the sign, not the pairing. A known-answer control (arm B = arm A reversed therefore difference 1.0) would fail on a real regression.

no test passes copy_groups= to bootstrap_interval and none passes scores_b, so the module's two unique capabilities - copy-group-aware resampling and the paired-difference interval - are unguarded; a regression that ignored copy_groups and treated every observation as its own group passes the whole new suite, as does one that dropped the scores_b branch.

the docstring pins a model version ('jev-1.13 is documented to lean to the first option'). The repository's naming rules bar version identifiers in source comments and docstrings, because the sentence rots on the next model bump; stating the mechanism ('a judge that leans to the first option') carries the rationale without the pin.
